declared_purpose: Automate app/product TikTok slideshow marketing through competitor research, image generation, text overlays, Postiz posting, analytics, and hook/CTA iteration. Conversion tracking and cross-posting are conditional extensions (SKILL.md:1-8, 21-32).

data_operations.operation: Collect, infer, and locally store onboarding information
data_operations.data_scope: App description, intended audience, problem, differentiator, website, monetization system, content preferences, and inferred app category.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Agent conversation; tiktok-marketing/app-profile.json, config.json, and strategy.json.
data_operations.condition: Entry explicitly prescribes collection and storage. Initializer creates empty templates; validator reads populated config, competitor research, and strategy files and prints a setup summary.

data_operations.operation: Persist and locally read authentication material
data_operations.source: User-supplied image-provider and Postiz API keys; optional RevenueCat secret key
data_operations.data_scope: imageGen.apiKey, postiz.apiKey, revenuecat.v2SecretKey, integration IDs, and project ID.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Config JSON and script memory. Separate RevenueCat setup instructions prescribe RC_API_KEY for an external helper.
data_operations.condition: Config storage is explicitly prescribed. Nonlocal image generation and Postiz require keys; bundled RevenueCat retrieval requires enabled plus v2SecretKey. Validator prints presence/status rather than key values.

data_operations.operation: Prescribe account activity and account connections
data_operations.data_scope: Warmup viewing, likes, follows, comments, optional casual videos; TikTok account connection and optional cross-platform connections.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: TikTok for engagement/content; Postiz and the selected platforms for account authorization.
data_operations.condition: Warmup is directed only for new or barely used accounts. TikTok connection is required; other platform connections are optional. Authorization scopes and platform-side processing are unspecified.

data_operations.operation: Research public competitors, infer patterns, and save findings
data_operations.source: Permission-gated browser research on TikTok and app stores; supplied competitor JSON
data_operations.data_scope: Niche searches; competitor handles, followers, content, URLs, engagement, posting patterns, sounds, pricing, and comment/review sentiment; inferred strengths and market gaps.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Search terms to the researched services; findings to tiktok-marketing/competitor-research.json and summaries to the caller/user.
data_operations.condition: Browser permission is explicitly required. The management script performs local JSON reads, additions, and summaries; it does not browse. Weekly updates are prescribed.

data_operations.operation: Send selected-provider image-generation requests and save images
data_operations.data_scope: Combined base and slide prompts, selected model, generation parameters, and the selected provider's API key. Templates can describe rooms or physical features, including age and ethnicity; use of real people's details is not established.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: OpenAI: https://api.openai.com/v1/images/generations; or Stability AI: https://api.stability.ai/v1/generation/{engineId}/text-to-image. Returned image bytes go to slideN_raw.png.
data_operations.condition: Only the selected provider receives requests. Each unfinished slide is generated; failures can trigger up to three attempts. Six consistent slides are prescribed; provider routing and retries are implementation choices.

data_operations.operation: Create and poll Replicate predictions; download output
data_operations.source: Combined slide prompts, config, and prediction responses
data_operations.data_scope: Prompt, model, image parameters, and Replicate API token; subsequently a returned prediction URL and image URL.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Creation: https://api.replicate.com/v1/predictions. Polling: prediction.urls.get receives the token. Download: prediction.output URL receives an unauthenticated fetch. Image bytes persist locally.
data_operations.condition: Replicate selected. Polling continues until success/failure. The source does not constrain returned URL origins; actual polling/download hosts are unresolved.

data_operations.operation: Copy local images and preserve completed generation outputs
data_operations.source: local_slideN.png and existing slideN_raw.png in the output directory
data_operations.data_scope: User-provided or previously generated image bytes.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local output directory; no generation-service disclosure on the local-provider path.
data_operations.condition: Local provider copies supplied images. Any provider skips an existing raw output larger than 10000 bytes. This implements the documented local option and resumable generation.

data_operations.operation: Read images and text, render overlays, and emit debugging output
data_operations.source: Local texts JSON and six matching image files
data_operations.data_scope: Slide pixels and overlay text; emoji removal and layout transformations.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Rendered PNG files in the input directory; full rendered text lines in stdout to the caller. No remote recipient is shown.
data_operations.condition: Overlay script invoked with exactly six text entries. Image/text processing is required for this workflow; full text debugging output is an implementation choice.

data_operations.operation: Upload slides and request a TikTok post through Postiz
data_operations.source: Local slide1.png through slide6.png, caption/title arguments, and config
data_operations.data_scope: Six image files and basenames; caption, title, integration ID, timestamp, privacy and TikTok settings; Postiz API key in authorization headers.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: https://api.postiz.com/public/v1/upload and /posts; requested destination is the configured TikTok integration.
data_operations.condition: Posting script invoked. Default privacy is SELF_ONLY and posting method is UPLOAD; config can override privacy. Entry requires draft review/music before publication. Script submits one TikTok integration, not a cross-post payload.

data_operations.operation: Return posting results and persist post metadata
data_operations.source: Postiz creation response and local posting inputs
data_operations.data_scope: Full creation response in stdout; post ID, caption, title, privacy, posting timestamp, and image count in metadata.
data_operations.condition: After the creation request returns. This is local output/persistence; the source shows no separate transmission of the response to another service.

data_operations.operation: Retrieve Postiz posts, account video candidates, and per-post analytics
data_operations.data_scope: Date-range post objects, connected release IDs, optional account video list, and engagement metrics. Postiz receives its API key, dates, and requested post IDs.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Postiz /posts, /posts/{id}/missing, and /analytics/post/{id}; responses return to the checker.
data_operations.condition: Runs even without --connect. TikTok and optional --app filtering happen locally. Candidate videos are fetched only with --connect and eligible unconnected posts. The two-hour cutoff governs connection eligibility, not analytics for already-connected posts.

data_operations.operation: Infer post/video correspondence and write release-ID associations
data_operations.source: Postiz publish dates, returned TikTok video IDs, and already-connected IDs
data_operations.data_scope: Chronologically inferred mapping of each eligible Postiz post to a TikTok video ID.
data_operations.condition: --connect plus unconnected posts older than two hours and available candidates. Matching uses the newest available IDs in chronological order; this is an inference and remote state mutation, distinct from analytics retrieval.

data_operations.source: Checker's selected connected posts and analytics responses
data_operations.data_scope: Post IDs, dates, truncated hook text, integration names, views, likes, comment/share counts, and release IDs.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: analytics-snapshot.json beside config, overwritten each run; selected details and summaries in caller stdout.
data_operations.condition: Checker completes analytics processing, including runs without --connect. No comment bodies or commenter identities are extracted here.

data_operations.operation: Retrieve daily post/platform analytics and maintain platform baselines
data_operations.source: Postiz APIs and previous local platform-stats.json
data_operations.data_scope: Date-range posts filtered locally to connected TikTok posts, per-post engagement, and every returned platform metric's latest total for each configured integration.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Postiz /posts, /analytics/post/{id}, and /analytics/{integrationId}; platform-stats.json beside config is read and overwritten.
data_operations.condition: Daily report invoked; default window is three days. All configured integration IDs are queried. Reporting uses platform Followers and Views to calculate growth.

data_operations.operation: Retrieve RevenueCat overview and transaction data
data_operations.data_scope: Overview metrics and transaction items; project ID, start timestamp, requested limit of 100, and V2 secret key sent in authenticated requests.
data_operations.condition: Requires revenuecat.enabled and v2SecretKey. Transactions request a lower time bound but no end bound or pagination. The endDate argument is not used in the request. Exact returned transaction fields are unspecified.

data_operations.operation: Persist raw RevenueCat results and reload previous results
data_operations.data_scope: Complete returned overview, returned transaction items, derived scalar metrics, and snapshot date.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: rc-snapshot.json beside config; local script memory on subsequent runs.
data_operations.condition: When RevenueCat is enabled, previous snapshot is read if present; successful retrieval overwrites it. Raw responses are not shown being sent to Postiz or image providers.

data_operations.operation: Infer conversions and funnel quality; accumulate performance history and reports
data_operations.source: Post analytics, RevenueCat transactions/scalar deltas, and existing hook-performance.json
data_operations.data_scope: Counts attributed to posts using 72-hour timestamp windows; inferred hook/CTA/app issues; historical hook text, metrics, CTA tags, and detected hook patterns.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: hook-performance.json and reports/YYYY-MM-DD.md beside config; report text to caller stdout. Entry additionally prescribes a summary to the user.
data_operations.condition: Daily report runs; conversion inferences depend on available RevenueCat data. Post dates are truncated to calendar dates, windows can overlap, and one configured project's conversion data is reused across app groups. These are estimates, not observed user-to-post links.

data_operations.source: RevenueCat integration reference; not implemented by the bundled daily-report path
data_operations.data_scope: Optional V1 subscriber lookup uses app_user_id and returns subscriptions, entitlements, purchase history, and management URL; optional V2 customer listing; dashboard scraping; webhook/manual events with type, timestamp, product, revenue, and currency.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: RevenueCat subscriber/customer endpoints; optional configured webhook server and tiktok-marketing/rc-events.json; browser/agent for dashboard data.
data_operations.condition: Only if a reference alternative is chosen. Authentication is described, but webhook handlers, customer-ID sourcing, dashboard automation, and an rc-events.json reader are not supplied.

data_operations.data_scope: UTM campaign labels and RevenueCat $attribution source information.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Campaign-link destination and RevenueCat attribution facilities if configured; exact destinations and collection implementation are absent.
data_operations.condition: Optional guidance. No bundled code constructs these links or demonstrates per-user click tracking.

potential_excess.data_scope: Complete RevenueCat overview and transaction items, including returned fields beyond the timestamps and scalar metrics actually consumed.
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Local rc-snapshot.json boundary; not an additional disclosure to Postiz.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Conversion attribution and comparisons require selected metrics and transaction timing. Raw-response persistence is an implementation choice, not an explicit requirement.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Retrieve sufficient conversion data, count transactions in attribution windows, and retain prior scalar values for deltas.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Process current transactions in memory, retain only necessary timestamp/count representations during calculation, and persist selected scalar baselines without raw overview or transaction objects.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Preserve all report metrics, 72-hour counts, and historical derived conversion counts; do not assume unknown transaction fields are needed by this implementation.

potential_excess.data_scope: Platform metric labels/totals other than Followers and Views.
potential_excess.condition: Daily report receives additional metric labels from any configured integration.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Platform growth reporting uses Followers and Views; storing every returned label is an implementation choice.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Keep the platform analytics requests and sufficient baselines to calculate follower/view growth.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Project each response to Followers and Views before persistence. This narrows extra retained data in a required action rather than removing the analytics action.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Retain both baseline fields for every intended integration; preserve separately required per-post likes, comments, and shares.

potential_excess.data_scope: A second copy of date-range Postiz post objects and a repeated authenticated request.
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Postiz GET /public/v1/posts and its response to scripts/check-analytics.js.
potential_excess.condition: Checker runs without --connect, or performs no release-ID mutation and requires no explicit concurrent-state refresh.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: The second fetch exists to obtain updated release IDs. Without mutations, the first response already supplies the analytics candidates.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Obtain post IDs/release IDs once and refresh when connection changes or uncertain external state require it.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Reuse the first response on unchanged paths; refetch after attempted writes when their outcome requires confirmation.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Preserve TikTok/app filtering, sorting, and analytics retrieval. Retain refreshes where a consistent current-state requirement makes them necessary.

potential_excess.data_scope: Returned post objects outside TikTok, and outside the selected app when checker --app is used.
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Account-wide Postiz /posts response entering checker or daily-report memory.
potential_excess.condition: The date range contains posts outside the intended subset. Requests supply dates only; filtering occurs after retrieval.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: These execution paths analyze TikTok posts; --app further narrows the checker's requested purpose. Broader acquisition is observable, but server-side narrowing support is unknown.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Retrieve relevant TikTok post IDs, timing, content, integration information, and release IDs needed for analytics and matching.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Use integration/platform predicates or a narrower endpoint if supported. Otherwise discard unrelated objects immediately and record that upstream acquisition cannot yet be narrowed.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Confirm API capabilities first; preserve all intended app groups and connected IDs needed to avoid duplicate video matches.

unknowns: External API schemas, permissions, filtering capabilities, actual response fields, retention, logging, and downstream processing are not supplied. These limit conclusions about upstream minimization and external persistence.

Posting success and actual destination are unresolved: scripts/post-to-tiktok.js:82 reads postiz.integrationId, while SKILL.md:358-364 and scripts/onboarding.js:145-146 use integrationIds.tiktok. The bundled payload contains one TikTok post; documented cross-posting and video behavior are not implemented there.

Cron execution, automatic connection orchestration, and delivery of user summaries are outside the supplied implementation. The prescribed cron runs daily-report.js (SKILL.md:319-327), which selects already-connected posts (scripts/daily-report.js:133-137).

The external RevenueCat skill/helper and MCP implementation are absent. V1 subscriber/dashboard/webhook alternatives in references/revenuecat-integration.md:20-46 differ from the bundled V2 API path in scripts/daily-report.js:54-98; their end-to-end data handling remains unresolved.

Batch generation is described as opt-in in SKILL.md:167-171, but scripts/generate-slides.js:185-201 only routes to the ordinary provider functions. No batch submission, storage, or deletion behavior is supplied.
Actual Replicate polling/download hosts are unknown because scripts/generate-slides.js:135-148 follows response-provided URLs. The token accompanies polling, not the image download.

Causal conversion attribution is unverified. Date truncation, overlapping windows, and project-wide conversion reuse can affect inferred post/app labels (scripts/daily-report.js:152-161, 283-299, 308-324, 375-409). No campaign/user join establishes which post caused a purchase.

No packaged cleanup establishes deletion of uploaded assets, generated slides, reports, hook history, or webhook logs. Snapshot overwrites are observable, but secure erasure, backups, and provider-side deletion lifecycles are unknown.
